analyst_view.overall: Early view: Fenerbahce (6th) are the league's top scorers with 29 and started the Emre Belozoglu era with a 5-0 win at Corum; they are also in the Champions League, where they beat Liverpool 3-2 on 4 November, so midweek rotation is possible. Promoted Erzurumspor (12th) under Serkan Ozbalta have scored ten goals in eleven games and lost their last two. Fenerbahce's absences (Asensio injured, Archie Brown suspended for Corum) need checking nearer the time.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Fenerbahce's games have averaged about 3.5 and Erzurumspor have conceded 17, so that is fair; Fenerbahce did lose at home to Goztepe on 2 November, a reminder that their home games are not always one-way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and I lean higher. Erzurumspor are likely to defend deep, and a Fenerbahce side with wide threats such as Greenwood and Oguz Aydin should force plenty of corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and I lean lower. A home game against a promoted side that will sit back should be fairly calm, with Fenerbahce on the ball for long spells and little reason for either side to make tactical fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, nearly 20 of them Fenerbahce's. That is a lot, but with Greenwood and Irfan Can in form, Lukaku leading the line and Erzurumspor short of attacking threat, it seems right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Fenerbahce's finishing at Corum was sharp and Erzurumspor will give little back, so around ten fits.
